story.title: WhatsApp’s new scheduled messages let you choose the right time to send

facts.text: WhatsApp users have long requested message scheduling to do things like set recurring reminders, manage time zones and handle business communications off-hours.
Now, it looks like Meta's messaging app will get that feature soon, according to a WhatsApp Android beta spotted by WaBetaInfo .
That opens up a dialog at the bottom of the screen, letting you choose the delivery date and time.
It also offers a dedicated section to manage scheduled messages before they're sent.
The message will be sent at the desired time, even if your device is offline.
As with any message, scheduled ones supports text, links, photos and videos, while being protected by end-to-end encryption.
Messages can be scheduled for as little as 10 minutes ahead of the current time, or up to two weeks in advance.
The feature is also compatible with group chats.
WhatsApp’s 3 billion users are getting an option that Meta says is one of the most requested features, with the ability to schedule messages in advance for both private conversations and group chats.
If you think of a text at an inconvenient time or don’t want to forget to fire off a birthday message at 4AM, you can draft it and set it to send anywhere from 10 minutes to two weeks later.
It’s one more way to show up for the people who matter to you, now at exactly the right time.
Most messaging platforms have had this for a very long time, but now it’s on WhatsApp too.
Meta: > To schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive.
But if you want or need to schedule a message for a contact or Whatsapp group to receive it on a certain day or time, several third-party applications on the market can serve you for this purpose.
These are the ones we recommend today: SKEDit Scheduling for Android and Shortcuts for iOS.

One of its best features is that it works not only for WhatsApp, but you can use this application to automate other mobile services such as scheduling a phone call, sending an SMS, sending an email or even uploading a Facebook post.
